messages.subject: error in filter the duplicate individuals
parts:
Hi!

When I filter the duplicated individuals, I get an error message:

Error in `[<-`(`*tmp*`, wh[i, 1], tozero, value = NA) :
(subscript) logical subscript too long


My code is:

for(i in 1:nrow(wh)) {
tozero <- !is.na(g[wh[i,1],]) & !is.na(g[wh[i,2],]) & g[wh[i,1],] != g[wh[i,2],];
mydata$geno[[1]]$data[wh[i,1],tozero] <- NA
}

So do anyone know how this error come?

Thanks a lot!

Ziming

Thanks for your fast reply, Karl!

First, I delete the individuals with less than 40000 markers:

mydata <- subset(mydata,ind=(ntyped(mydata)>40000))

Then I delete the markers that present in less than 55 individuals:

todrop <- names(nt.bymar[nt.bymar < 55])
mydata <- drop.markers(mydata, towrope)

Then I need to delete the duplicated individuals:

cg <- comparegeno(my data)  #compare the genotype by pairs of individuals
wh <- which(cg > 0.9, arr=TRUE) #to select the pairs with >90% similarity
wh <- wh[wh[,1] < wh[,2],] #to delete the duplicated row in wh. Am I right?

for(i in 1:nrow(wh)) {
  tozero <- !is.na(g[wh[i,1],]) & !is.na(g[wh[i,2],]) & g[wh[i,1],] != g[wh[i,2],]

mapthis$geno[[1]]$data[wh[i,1],tozero] <- NA

Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: error in filter the duplicate individuals
parts:
If you're trying to filter the duplicate individuals, you can skip that loop with the "tozero" business. That code is for removing any genotypes that are mismatched between the individuals.

To remove the duplicate individuals, use subset.  Something like this:

cg <- comparegeno(mapthis)
wh <- which(cg > 0.9, arr=TRUE)

mapthis <- subset(mapthis, ind = -wh[,2])

karl

messages.subject: Re: error in filter the duplicate individuals
parts:
I should also add: that code with the "tozero" business is taken from page 7 of the Genetic Map Construction tutorial. And at that point the mapthis object had just one chromosome (because we hadn't yet inferred the linkage groups) and also the g object was the matrix of genotypes, for that one and only chromosome.

I you wanted to do that sort of thing (for each pair of duplicates, remove any marker genotypes where they are discordant) in the case that there is more than one chromosome, you'd need an additional look over chromosomes:

for(j in chrnames(mapthis)) {
    g <- pull.geno(mapthis, chr=j)

for(i in 1:nrow(wh)) {
        tozero <- !is.na(g[wh[i,1],]) & !is.na(g[wh[i,2],]) & g[wh[i,1],] != g[wh[i,2],]

mapthis$geno[[j]]$data[wh[i,1], tozero] <- NA
    }
}

karl
